observations: Torah LM2 #70 is one of the shortest teachings in Likutay Moharan — three sentences presenting a single universal principle about the proportionality between spiritual greatness and the distance at which one must seek one's 'desired thing' (מְבֻקָּשׁ). The teaching introduces several concepts (הַצּוֹמֵחַ, בְּהֵמָה, בֶּן-אָדָם, מֹשֶׁה, מִדְיָן) but NONE of them are connected using explicit bechina language. There is no 'X הוא בְּחִינַת Y' formula anywhere in the text. The entire teaching is structured as a proportional analogy: as level of being increases, distance of the מְבֻקָּשׁ increases. This is not bechina (shared nature/identity) but an eitza-type (structural-proportional) relationship. To propose a new package requires at least 3 concepts connected by explicit bechina language forming an independent domain — this Torah provides none. No new package is warranted. The teaching's conceptual content is entirely structural/analogical, appropriate for eitza edges only if the dataset were to be enriched in the future.
